changes: Notes: syedaṃ(!) is most likely asyedaṃ with the first syllable lost (asyedaṃ pustakaṃ … -sya, the standard ownership formula); dropped the 'svam idaṃ' alternative.
Notes: hedged the identification of Trivikramasena's dynasty and kingdom, since the colophon does not name a kingdom.
Notes: added that the wrote_for relation is inferred from the two sentences standing next to each other, not stated outright.
Persons, roles, titles and the empty date and place confirmed as they were.

notes: The colophon has no date or place. syedaṃ(!) is most likely asyedaṃ with the first syllable lost: 'this book belongs to King Trivikramasena'. Trivikramasena was a king of one of the Sena lines; Tanahun and Makwanpur are both possible, but the colophon names no kingdom, so the identification is unconfirmed. The wrote_for relation (the scribe copying for the king) is inferred because the scribe statement and the ownership statement stand next to each other; the colophon does not say it directly. 'Pantha' (Panta/Pant) is read as a brahmin family name or title of the scribe. The author's name is also written paḍita(!)rājajagaṃnnātha(!) in the first vilāsa colophon.
